reviews.one_line_contribution: A carrier-contrast experiment: the same planted ALFWorld trait is put either in a self-teacher's retrieved memory (identical weights) or in a rate-matched LoRA teacher's parameters, and four distillation objectives (SFT, sanitised SFT, on-policy reverse-KL, span-masked reverse-KL) test whether subliminal transfer through semantically clean tokens requires a parameter-carried trait, extending the subliminal-learning question to agent trajectories and, for the first time as far as I could verify, to a masked on-policy objective.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Two, and the second is the one that hurts. (a) Subliminal Transfer of Unsafe Behaviors in AI Agent Distillation (arXiv:2604.15559, verified on S2 via title search, 2026-04-16, 4 citations; note the `paper 2604.15559` lookup returned 'not found on S2 or HF' for me, so the proposal's claimed verification route is not reproducible) already establishes that agent behaviours survive keyword sanitation under trajectory distillation and that sanitation is an insufficient defence; its abstract advertises 'two complementary experimental settings', which the proposal asserts are both parameter-carried SFT without evidence that it read them. (b) More damaging: 'You Didn't Have to Say It like That: Subliminal Learning from Faithful Paraphrases' (arXiv:2603.09517, verified on S2, 2026-03-10, 4 citations) reports that a teacher **system-prompted** to love an animal — i.e. a context-carried trait in a model whose weights are identical to the student's base — raises the student's preference by up to 19 pp through paraphrases that survive aggressive fidelity filtering. That is the proposal's memory-carried leg, in text, with the answer already 'yes, it transfers through clean tokens'. The proposal cites 2603.09517 in one clause as merely 'disputing the channel' and never confronts it, and it also mischaracterises Cloud et al. (2507.14805, verified) as requiring 'a teacher whose parameters differ in the trait direction' when that paper's animal-trait teachers are themselves prompt-induced. The 'parameter-proximity account' that P3 is built to defend is therefore closer to a strawman than to a live hypothesis, which is what cuts novelty: what survives as genuinely untested is the on-policy/masked-KL leg (2609.01091 verified, and titled 'under SFT Distillation'; 2606.00831 verified, LoRA/SFT only; 2605.16826 verified, gives the objective taxonomy but no traits) and the agent-memory instantiation.
reviews.strongest_objection: The MC null is close to definitional, and the MC-vs-PC contrast is confounded by breadth rather than by carrier. T1's trait is a single action span; SFT-clean deletes exactly that span and OPD-masked zeroes the KL on exactly that span, so for a context-triggered, decision-point-local trait there is almost nothing left in the data by which MC could differ from MC-0 — the brief's own rule forbids 'a prediction entailed by a definition'. Meanwhile the PC teacher, LoRA-trained on the rewritten walkthroughs, has a trait that is diffuse across its whole token distribution, which is precisely the quantity the drift account (2609.01091) says drives transfer. Rate-matching PC to MC on the decision-point trait rate does not equalise that diffuseness, so 'PC transfers, MC does not' is equally well explained by 'a globally shifted output distribution transfers, a locally triggered one does not' — a conclusion about trait geometry, not about weights-vs-context, and one that would not license the paper's safety headline about memory sanitation. Secondarily, the P3 equivalence test's unit of inference is the training run, not the episode: two training seeds give ~1 df for the seed variance the design proposes to fold into the CI, so the ±5 pp margin is nominal, and this is the same failure-to-reject-read-as-a-null that sank the archived harm_does_not_distill. Third, everything (both teachers, all students) is QLoRA rank 32, inside the exact regime that 2606.00831 (verified) calls an artifact — so P1's positive control and P2's on-policy comparison could both be adapter-specific.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: (1) Reframe against 2603.09517 rather than against parameter-proximity: state that context-carried transfer through clean tokens is already demonstrated in text with a system-prompted teacher, and make the contribution the conditions under which it does or does not reproduce for retrieved agent memory and for masked on-policy objectives. Drop the assertive title. (2) Add a trait whose expression is not confined to one deletable span (e.g. a persistent phrasing/verbosity or receptacle-preference disposition realised across many tokens per episode), so that sanitisation removes the trait's *label* but not its only carrier; without such a trait the MC null is uninformative. (3) Make the unit of inference the training run: 4-5 training seeds on the two arms that carry P3, and report the equivalence test on the seed-level mean, or drop the equivalence claim and report the MC-vs-PC difference as the estimand. (4) Match diffuseness, not just the decision-point rate: report a teacher-side measure of how much of the whole token distribution is shifted (e.g. mean per-token KL of MC and PC teachers against their controls on identical rollouts) and use it, not the trait rate alone, as the matching axis. (5) One full-parameter or higher-rank arm to show P1/P2 are not the LoRA artifact of 2606.00831. (6) Read and report what 2604.15559's second experimental setting actually is before claiming it tests only parameter-carried SFT.
reviews.missing_baseline: An instruction/system-prompt-induced trait teacher — identical weights, trait in the prompt rather than in retrieved items — run through the same four objectives. It is the exact construction of 2603.09517 and Cloud et al.'s prompted teachers, so it is the only arm that separates 'retrieved memory does not transmit dispositions' from 'context of any kind does not transmit dispositions on this backbone', and it converts a possible MC null from an isolated negative into a replication failure of a published positive. The proposal relegates it to a fallback if Gate 0 fails. Also absent: a deletion placebo for SFT-clean (the OPD side gets a random-span mask placebo, but SFT-clean deletes a step, changing sequence length and the state distribution, with no random-step-deletion control), and any non-LoRA transfer arm given that 2606.00831 is cited as a live threat.
reviews.preprint_collision: No verified collision — I found no preprint making this proposal's central claim, so novelty is not capped on that ground, but the check is incomplete in substance rather than in form. Queries, all answered by channel (a), the s2cli command (WebSearch unavailable this session): [1] 'subliminal trait transfer context-carried teacher on-policy distillation masked tokens' --recent → 2606.22019, 2606.00995, 2507.14805, 2607.19046 (Contrastive On-Policy Distillation), 2606.30626 (DOPD), 2605.30833, 2605.10889; none tests trait transfer under an on-policy objective. [2] 'subliminal transfer unsafe behaviors agent trajectory distillation sanitized keywords' (all years) → verified 2604.15559 on S2, 2026-04-16, 4 citations, abstract mentions 'two complementary experimental settings' and 'data sanitation is an insufficient defense'. [3] 'system-prompted teacher transmits trait to student identical base weights filtered data' (all years) → nothing beyond 2606.22019, 2606.00995 and 2510.04340 (Inoculation Prompting). [4] 'retrieved memory bank plants disposition agent self-distillation internalizes behavior beyond procedure' --recent → 2608.07169 (Agent Memory Distillation), 2607.01480 (PMD), 2607.10608 (Compliance Trap), 2602.04942; none asks what a memory-conditioned teacher transmits besides procedure. [5] 'prompt-induced versus finetuned teacher trait carrier comparison subliminal learning shared initialization' --recent → 2605.12798 (Emergent and Subliminal Misalignment Through the Lens of Data-Mediated Transfer) and re-hits; no carrier contrast. ID verification: 2606.00831 (2026-05-30, S2, 4 cit), 2603.09517 (2026-03-10, S2, 4 cit), 2609.01091 (2026-09-01, S2), 2605.16826 (2026-05-16, HF), 2507.14805 and 2606.22019 all verified; 2604.15559 could NOT be verified through `s2cli paper` (returned 'not found on S2 or HF') and was verified only by title search, contradicting the proposal's claim to have verified it by paper lookup. The proposal's own check ran only two queries and, more importantly, did not search the construction that most threatens it — a system-prompted, identical-weight teacher — even though it cites 2603.09517, whose result (context-carried trait transferring through aggressively filtered paraphrases, +19 pp) is the closest thing to the headline null being pre-falsified in the text domain. Reporting that paper as 'disputing the channel' rather than as a direct threat to P3 is the weakness in this check.
